# fulfillment-service

Node.js, no dependencies. `npm test` runs the suite.

Quantities are integers. Times are epoch milliseconds. Money is integer minor units (cents).

## Stock

`new Stock(levels)` copies levels `{warehouse, sku, onHand, held, priority}`. `level(sku, warehouse)`
returns the live level. Available quantity at a level is `onHand - held` (never below 0).

## Allocation

`allocate(levels, quantity)` walks the levels in ascending `priority`, ties broken by `warehouse`
id ascending, taking up to the *available* quantity from each. It returns
`{lines: [{warehouse, quantity}], backorderQuantity}` where `backorderQuantity` is what could not be
allocated. Levels with nothing available produce no line.

## Reservations

`new ReservationBook(stock, clock, audit)`.

- `reserve({orderId, sku, quantity, customerTier})`: `orderId` and `sku` must be non-empty strings
  (`invalid_request`) and `quantity` a positive safe integer (`invalid_quantity`). Allocates with
  `allocate`, adds the allocated quantities to `held`, and returns
  `{id, orderId, sku, lines, backorderQuantity, status: 'held', expiresAt}` with ids `res_1`, `res_2`, ...
  Holds last 10 minutes (600,000 ms) for every customer tier. Partial allocation is allowed; the
  remainder is reported as `backorderQuantity`.
- A hold expires when `clock() >= expiresAt`. Expired holds stop counting toward `held` and get
  status `expired`. Every operation first expires due holds.
- `release(id)`: a held reservation becomes `released` and its quantities leave `held`. Releasing a
  reservation that is not held changes nothing and returns it as is. Unknown ids throw
  `reservation_not_found`.
- `commit(id)`: a held reservation becomes `committed`; its quantities leave both `held` and
  `onHand`. Expired reservations throw `reservation_expired`; any other non-held status throws
  `reservation_not_held`.
- `available(sku)` sums available quantity across the sku's levels.
- Returned reservations are copies. Each state change records an audit entry
  `{type, reservationId, at}` with type `reserved`, `released`, `expired` or `committed`.

## Audit

`AuditLog#record(entry)` stores a copy. `entries()` returns copies; nothing a caller does to an entry
or the returned array changes the log.

## API

`handleReserve(book, body)` returns `{status: 201, body: reservation}`; `invalid_request` and
`invalid_quantity` map to 400 `{error}`, `insufficient_stock` to 409 `{error}`, anything else to
500 `{error: 'internal'}`.

## Pricing

`priceOrder({lines, coupons = []})` with lines `{unitMinor, quantity}` (non-empty array, non-negative
safe-integer unit, positive safe-integer quantity, otherwise `invalid_order`).

- Coupons are `{type: 'percent', value}` with an integer value 1–100, or `{type: 'fixed', value}`
  with a positive safe-integer value. Anything else throws `invalid_coupon`.
- Starting from the subtotal, all percent coupons apply first in the given order, each removing
  `roundHalfEven(total * value, 100)` from the running total; then fixed coupons subtract their value.
- The total never goes below 0. Returns `{subtotalMinor, discountMinor, totalMinor}` with
  `discountMinor = subtotalMinor - totalMinor`.

issue.title: Checkout produces negative totals and misapplies stacked coupons
Checkout produces negative totals and misapplies stacked coupons

args.body:
Fixed in commit f35f495 on main.

Root causes:
1. Coupons were applied in whatever order they were given, instead of "all percent first, then all fixed" as the README requires — so orders with the same two coupons priced differently depending on submission order.
2. Percent discounts used Math.round instead of the spec's roundHalfEven.
3. Total wasn't clamped at 0, so stacked fixed coupons could push totalMinor negative (the "we paid the customer" bug).
4. Coupons weren't validated at all — invalid coupon shapes/values silently applied instead of throwing invalid_coupon.

Added regression tests in tests/pricing.test.mjs covering order-independence, rounding, zero-floor clamping, and invalid coupon rejection. Full suite run: pricing tests all green (reservations.test.mjs has unrelated pre-existing failures tracked under INV-44).

Resuming INV-44 now.

  `allocate`, adds the allocated quantities to `held`, and returns
  `{id, orderId, sku, lines, backorderQuantity, status: 'held', expiresAt}` with ids `res_1`, `res_2`, ...
  Reservations are all-or-nothing: if the order cannot be fully allocated, nothing is held and

- allocation: available quantity per level now accounts for held stock

  broken by ascending warehouse id per the README.
- reservations: expireDue now expires holds when clock() >= expiresAt
  (was strictly >, leaking holds past their TTL).
- reservations: commit() now runs expireDue() first so an expired hold
  is correctly rejected with reservation_expired instead of being
  committed after it should have freed its stock.
- reservations: release() no longer decrements held stock a second time
  when called on an already-released or committed reservation; any
  non-held status now returns unchanged, per the README.
- reservations: quantity validation now requires a safe integer, not
  just quantity > 0 (rejects e.g. 1.5).
- reservations: reserve() is now all-or-nothing per product decision
  (Jordan, INV-44) — throws insufficient_stock and holds nothing if the
  order can't be fully allocated; successful reservations always report
  backorderQuantity 0.
- reservations: hold TTL is 30 minutes for customerTier 'vip' and 10
  minutes for every other/missing tier, per product decision (Jordan,
  INV-44).
- audit: record() stores a shallow copy and entries() returns copies,
  so callers mutating an entry or the returned array can no longer
  rewrite audit history after the fact.
- README updated to document the two product-approved contract changes
  (all-or-nothing reserve, VIP hold duration).

The flash sale oversold. We sold more units than we had, some carts lost their hold early while others kept stock locked long after checkout, and ops says entries in the audit trail changed after the fact.

Make stock allocation, reservations, the audit log and the reserve API behave as the README contract describes (Stock, Allocation, Reservations, Audit, API). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Jordan is the fulfillment product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Lena is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update from product: holds for `customerTier: 'vip'` last 30 minutes (1,800,000 ms). Every other tier, including a missing tier, keeps 10 minutes. This replaces the README reservation-duration rule for VIP customers only; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

args.body:
Fixed and committed on main (a24001e + 31ed8e9).

Root causes of the oversell:
- Allocation used raw `onHand` instead of `onHand - held`, so it could allocate stock that was already held by another order.
- Hold expiry used `clock() > expiresAt` instead of `>=`, so holds outlived their 10-minute TTL by however long it took for the next operation to run.
- `release()` decremented `held` again when called on an already-released or committed reservation (e.g. a retried release call), incorrectly freeing capacity that wasn't actually free.
- `commit()` didn't expire due holds first, so an expired hold could still be committed instead of being rejected.
- `quantity` validation accepted non-integers like 1.5.
- Audit log stored/returned live references instead of copies, so entries could be edited after the fact.

Also implemented both product updates from this thread:
- `reserve` is now all-or-nothing: throws `insufficient_stock` (already mapped to 409 by the API) and holds nothing if the order can't be fully allocated; successful reservations always have `backorderQuantity: 0`.
- VIP holds now last 30 minutes; every other/missing tier stays at 10 minutes.

README updated to reflect both product decisions. 16 regression tests added covering every fix (tests/reservations.test.mjs), full suite green.

args.text: INV-44 (flash sale oversell) is fixed, tested, and committed — marked done. Root causes: allocation ignored held stock, hold expiry used `>` instead of `>=`, release() double-decremented held on repeat/committed calls, commit() skipped expiring due holds, and the audit log wasn't storing copies (so it could be edited after the fact). Also rolled in Jordan's two product updates: reserve is now all-or-nothing (insufficient_stock if it can't be fully filled) and VIP holds last 30min vs 10min for everyone else. 16 new regression tests, full suite green.
